newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends week stable, nickel stumbles.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends week stable, nickel stumbles.

text.p: Copper prices lost touch with new one-year highs by the end of business on Friday, while nickel slid to the lowest in six weeks after concerns about a weekend strike lifted.
Building on this month's steady gains, three months copper pushed up to a fresh high of $2,548 per tonne in brisk ring afternoon trading on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
But end-of-week book squaring and profit-taking pushed prices lower by the end of the kerb.

It finished at $2,529 per tonne, a gain of just $1 from Thursday's finish. Resistance of $2,550 will remain key, but in the case of a correction in current overbought conditions, strong support is expected at $2,515 and $2,500.
Cash to threes backwardation eased by some $10 to $60/$70.

Nickel prices, meanwhile, plummeted to finish at a six-week low of $7,200, down $80, following news that Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd had reached a tentative agreement with the union representing 4,700 workers at its Ontario division.
Unionised workers were set to go on strike at midnight on Saturday, May 31, if a tentative agreement had not been reached.
"Nickel has certainly not been helped by the tentative agreement, which makes it much less likely that there will be a strike. It was looking pretty shaky already," an analyst said.
The union will still need to ratify the agreement.
In the event of further losses next week, nickel will be eyeing support at $7,110, the low from mid-April.
Aluminium failed to make any upside progress within its $1,610-$1,650 price range, despite a sizeable 4,250-tonne drop in LME stocks, and ended in the minus column.
It was down $3 at $1,619, although off the day's lows.
Tin, initially blasted by fund selling on Thursday, ended still lower at $5,570, down $30.
Below these levels, which were already the lowest in more than two years, tin was seen testing support at $5,550 and possibly lower, chartists said.
Zinc also eased $12 to $1,345, with a rise in stocks and overbought technical indicators suggesting a downward correction may be in the offing.
Lead was generally quiet but ended easier with the others at $633, down $7.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,485/$1,490, compared to $1,492/$1,497.
